claim.quote: We report here the detection of such photons from an extragalactic source, the giant elliptical galaxy Markarian 421.

key_value_text.quote: The flux above 0.5 TeV is 0.3 of that from the Crab Nebula.
key_value_text.value: Flux above 0.5 TeV is 0.3 of that from the Crab Nebula

name: Whipple detects TeV photons from the active galaxy Markarian 421
notes: No significance is recorded: the abstract text as retrieved garbles the significance symbol ("6er above background"), so the value is not copied.
The Whipple page states "the first extragalactic source detected at TeV energies by a ground-based instrument in 1992 (Punch et al 1992)".

summary.plain: The Whipple telescope detected TeV photons from Markarian 421, a galaxy with an active nucleus, the first source beyond our Galaxy seen at these energies.
summary.technical: Observations in March-June 1992 with the Whipple Observatory gamma-ray telescope show a signal from Mrk 421 (redshift 0.031) with a flux above 0.5 TeV of 0.3 that of the Crab Nebula; the source position agrees within the 6 arcminute uncertainty.

title: Detection of TeV photons from the active galaxy Markarian 421
why_it_matters: The Whipple page records it as the first extragalactic source detected at TeV energies by a ground-based instrument, in 1992, and the abstract links the non-detection of more distant active galaxies to absorption of TeV photons by extragalactic starlight.
